issue_context.title: Orphaned device after removing Bitwarden add-on
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I tried the Bitwarden (Vaulwarden) from Home Assistant Community Add-ons. After testing it, I chose to remove it.
The add-on is removed, but a device called Bitwarden (Vaultwarden) remains in the devices list.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.6.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Bitwarden (Vaultwarden)

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
21-06-24 19:07:45 INFO (SyncWorker_1) [supervisor.docker.interface] Stopping addon_a0d7b954_bitwarden application
21-06-24 19:07:49 INFO (SyncWorker_1) [supervisor.docker.interface] Cleaning addon_a0d7b954_bitwarden application
21-06-24 19:07:59 INFO (SyncWorker_1) [supervisor.docker.interface] Removing image ghcr.io/hassio-addons/bitwarden/armv7 with latest and 0.11.0
21-06-24 19:07:59 INFO (MainThread) [supervisor.addons.addon] Removing add-on data folder /data/addons/data/a0d7b954_bitwarden
21-06-24 19:07:59 INFO (MainThread) [supervisor.addons] Add-on 'a0d7b954_bitwarden' successfully removed
```


### Additional information

_No response_
comments: Dev note: The issue here is that the device is not cleaned up from the device registry if the add-on is uninstalled. A possible solution is to check which add-ons are installed on the system when the integration sets up, and remove unknown add-ons/devices from the registry.

Hey there @home-assistant/supervisor, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`hassio`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L197) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
If I'm not mistaken, the supervisor fire an event over the websocket on add-on install/uninstall, we should be able to trigger cleanup/registration on that event
I was wrong, looks like that was never implemented <https://github.com/home-assistant/supervisor/pull/2978>
It might still miss such an event, so a cleanup task in general on setup might be a good start.
I'd say both, run check/cleanup/add on init and on received event

review_comments: Looks like we don't need to copy to list.
Did not even notice that, will do a followup 👍
